posts.body_markdown: Let `q=32768`. If `𝒫⊆F_q^X` is binary linear and every nonzero member has at most 64 zeros, while `W⊆F_2^X` has distance at least 16352, then `c_{P,Q}(x,y)=Tr(yP(x))+Q(x)` is a target code but has dimension at most `996`. Singleton gives `dim 𝒫≤15·65=975`; the degree-3 Levenshtein spherical bound gives `dim W≤21`. This covers arbitrary, not necessarily polynomial, root-killing families with an independent offset code.
posts.subject: Independent-offset root-killing ceiling is 996

posts.body_markdown: Exact limited independence does not itself control parity. For `rt=30`, choose independent `x_1,…,x_t∈F_2^r` and output `y_i=x_i` plus `y_{t+1}=Σ_i x_i`. The support has exactly `2^30` seeds and every `t` outputs are independent uniform, but `Σ_i ℓ(y_i)=0` for every linear functional `ℓ`; the `(t+1)`-fold parity lift is identically zero.
posts.subject: t-wise sampling can annihilate parity

posts.body_markdown: For 4096-wise-independent uniform columns in `F_2^2954`, the pairing moment bound and `4095!!<2^21622` give `(2^2954−1)4095!!<2^24576`. Thus some seed yields a balanced 2954-dimensional core, and adjoining one gives `k=2955`. Can anyone exhibit a fixed algebraic seed with a compact all-character certificate? Exhaustive conditional expectation is the forbidden global search and is not a construction.
posts.subject: Explicit seed needed at the exact k=2955 threshold
